title: The compiler seals the whole DAG: an INITIAL run admits N nodes, the mission asks for the complete graph
description:
SPIDR child 1 of parent task-4423d2a4c3084d579c132b253d36b502 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-04). Dependency-free LEAF; children 2-5 build on it.

OWNER RULING (task-4423d2a4 comment-fbe64776, 2026-09-04, relayed from the owner's words "lift the fence"): LIFT THE ONE-NODE FENCE. An INITIAL run seals the WHOLE graph. The parent's description still argues for keeping the fence and is SUPERSEDED by that comment; its DoD 1 and DoD 5 are replaced.

Do not "restore" it.
- WHAT ACTUALLY REFUSES: `apps/daemon/src/planning/compile-dispatcher.ts:196-197` `if (nodes.length > 1) return refused("SUBMIT_DECOMPOSITION_MULTI_NODE_INITIAL")`. The code is rostered one place: `SUBMIT_DECOMPOSITION_CODES` at compile-dispatcher.ts:47-51 (the constant runs 47..~52; the literal is line 51).
- THE MISSION STILL TELLS SEATS THE OPPOSITE: `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-mission-text.ts:123` "dependsOn}]}}. Plan the SMALLEST COMPLETE SLICE: exactly ONE node in an" (the sentence wraps past 123 - read the surrounding array, do not sed a single line).
- THE DOWNSTREAM MACHINERY IS ALREADY MULTI-NODE AND NEEDS NO CHANGE: `compile-dispatcher.ts:209-228` already reads, validates and seals per-node `dependsOn`; `apps/daemon/src/planning/compiled-authority-bodies.ts:62-70` already refuses an unknown dependency, a self-edge and a dependency on the completion node (COMPILED_PLAN_MALFORMED) and already refuses an uncovered criterion (COMPILED_PLAN_CRITERION_UNBOUND, lines 84-92). Multi-node propose was proven live once already (memory initial-run-seals-one-node-by-core-design).

SOURCE-TEXT ASSERTER (global rail 23 enumeration, `git grep -l SUBMIT_DECOMPOSITION_MULTI_NODE_INITIAL` over the whole tree = exactly 3 hits): compile-dispatcher.ts:51 (roster), compile-dispatcher.ts:197 (the refusal), and `apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-close-readiness.test.ts:18` - a PROSE COMMENT that states the refusal as a premise. NOTE that file is currently dirty in the shared checkout (peer WIP) - edit only the comment lines you own, never revert or stash the rest (global rail 5).
definitionOfDone: `apps/daemon/src/planning/compile-dispatcher.ts` admits N>=1 execution-bearing nodes: the `nodes.length > 1` arm is deleted and `SUBMIT_DECOMPOSITION_MULTI_NODE_INITIAL` is REMOVED from `SUBMIT_DECOMPOSITION_CODES`. `git grep -c SUBMIT_DECOMPOSITION_MULTI_NODE_INITIAL` over the tree returns 0 hits in production source (the goal-close-readiness.test.ts prose comment is rewritten, not left stating the retired rule).

A dispatcher test submits a THREE-node structure with a real HARD chain (c depends on b, b depends on a) and asserts the submission SEALS: assert the returned graphContentHash/submissionHash are present and the disposition is DECIDED - not merely that it did not refuse. A second arm submits one node and still seals (N=1 is not regressed).

The refusal arms that MUST survive are pinned by code, each asserting the specific code and layer: an unknown `dependsOn` target and a self-edge both refuse COMPILED_PLAN_MALFORMED; a criterion bound by no node refuses COMPILED_PLAN_CRITERION_UNBOUND. These are the fence that replaces the node-count fence - a plan whose DAG is incoherent must still not seal.

`apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-mission-text.ts` tells the planning seat to plan the COMPLETE graph as a dependency DAG: every criterion of the approved revision covered by exactly one node, `dependsOn` naming hard build order. A mission-text test pins the NEW sentence verbatim and asserts the string "exactly ONE node" no longer appears anywhere in the produced mission.

Mutation drill recorded in a step note: re-insert `if (nodes.length > 1) return refused(...)` in compile-dispatcher.ts, confirm the three-node sealing test goes RED, restore, and prove the restore with `git diff -- apps/daemon/src/planning/compile-dispatcher.ts` (tracked file; quote the empty diff).

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/core test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`. Note explicitly that `pnpm test` covers no apps/** (global rail 18).

implementationPlan.description: VERIFY AND RE-MEASURE, NO EDITS. The fence-lift ruling is the authority for this row; confirm it still describes disk before changing anything. Run and quote in a step note: (a) `git grep -n SUBMIT_DECOMPOSITION_MULTI_NODE_INITIAL -- '*.ts'` — expect EXACTLY 3 hits, all named in this plan: compile-dispatcher.ts:51 (the roster entry), compile-dispatcher.ts:197 (the refusal), goal-close-readiness.test.ts:18 (a prose comment). A FOURTH hit means a peer added a consumer while this row waited — stop and report rather than taking the extra path. (b) `git grep -n 'SUBMIT_DECOMPOSITION_CODES' -- '*.ts'` — expect exactly ONE hit, its own declaration; there is no external scanner and no length pin over this roster (measured at plan time). (c) `sed -n '125,155p' packages/core/src/planning/planning-run-submission.ts` — confirm `finalize` still refuses only `bearing.length === 0`, i.e. core will ACCEPT the multi-node runs this row starts sealing. If core has regained a node-count arm, STOP and report blocked: this row must not edit core. (d) `git status --porcelain` on the five files in this plan — `goal-close-readiness.test.ts` is expected DIRTY with peer WIP; record its state now so step 5 can prove it touched only its own line.

TESTS FIRST, RUN RED. apps/daemon/src/planning/compile-dispatcher.test.ts (292 lines today; `structureOf()` at :160 currently takes no arguments and builds a single node — generalise it to take a node list, keeping every existing call site's behaviour byte-identical so the INITIAL arms in `describe("runSubmitDecomposition")` at :194-292 stay green). Add: (1) THE SEALING ARM — submit a THREE-node structure with a real HARD chain (c dependsOn b, b dependsOn a; criteria split across the three so every contract criterion is bound exactly once) and assert it SEALS: `ok === true`, and BOTH `graphContentHash` and `submissionHash` are present non-empty strings, and the disposition is DECIDED. Asserting only "did not refuse" is not enough — a refusal arm that stops returning a code would pass that. (2) THE N=1 REGRESSION ARM — a one-node structure still seals, so lifting the fence did not trade one count limit for another. Run both RED before touching production: (1) must fail with `SUBMIT_DECOMPOSITION_MULTI_NODE_INITIAL` and (2) must already pass.

PIN THE FENCE THAT REPLACES THE NODE-COUNT FENCE, still in compile-dispatcher.test.ts, still before production changes. Lifting the count limit is only safe because DAG coherence is already enforced by `apps/daemon/src/planning/compiled-authority-bodies.ts` — measured at plan time: :62-70 refuses an unknown `dependsOn` target, a self-edge, and a dependency on the completion node with COMPILED_PLAN_MALFORMED; :84-92 refuses a criterion satisfied by no node with COMPILED_PLAN_CRITERION_UNBOUND. Write one arm per refusal, each asserting the SPECIFIC code AND the layer the dispatcher reports (global rail 1 — a bare "it refused" arm is vacuous here, because several layers can refuse a malformed structure and the wrong one answering would keep the test green). Cover at minimum: an unknown dependsOn target; a self-edge; a criterion bound by no node. These arms are this row's real deliverable — they are what makes a multi-node plan safe to seal — so write them even though they exercise code you are not editing. Run them: they should PASS already; if one does not, the coherence fence is weaker than measured and this row must report blocked rather than lift the count fence on top of it.

MINIMUM IMPLEMENTATION, turning step 2 green. apps/daemon/src/planning/compile-dispatcher.ts (341 lines; the file stays well under the 400 cap because this step only DELETES): (a) delete the `if (nodes.length > 1) return refused("SUBMIT_DECOMPOSITION_MULTI_NODE_INITIAL");` arm at :196-197 together with the 5-line comment block above it at :191-195 — that comment states the retired core rule ("an INITIAL run seals exactly ONE execution-bearing node") and must not survive as a false premise; replace it with one sentence saying node COUNT is unconstrained and DAG coherence is enforced by compiled-authority-bodies. (b) delete the `"SUBMIT_DECOMPOSITION_MULTI_NODE_INITIAL",` entry from `SUBMIT_DECOMPOSITION_CODES` at :51. Change NOTHING else: the per-node `dependsOn` read, validation and sealing at :209-228 already handle N nodes and are what the sealing arm exercises. Do not touch packages/core (task rail 1). Re-run the step-2 and step-3 arms: all green.

THE MISSION STOPS ASKING FOR ONE NODE. apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-mission-text.ts: the sentence lives across :122-127 as array elements, not on one line — read the whole literal and rewrite the block, do not sed line 123. Today it reads "Plan the SMALLEST COMPLETE SLICE: exactly ONE node in an INITIAL run (the daemon refuses more - growth is the expansion machinery's), its criterionIds covering every criterion of the approved revision." Replace with instructions to plan the COMPLETE graph as a dependency DAG: every criterion of the approved revision covered by exactly one node across the whole structure, and `dependsOn` naming hard build order between nodes. Keep the surrounding payload-shape sentences and the "never authority bytes" and RUN_POLICY_UNCLASSIFIABLE sentences unchanged. Then apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-mission-text.test.ts:37-38 — the ONLY place in the tree that pins these words (measured: `git grep -n 'SMALLEST COMPLETE SLICE\|exactly ONE node'` returns just the source and these two lines). Replace both pins with a verbatim pin on the new sentence, and ADD `expect(text).not.toContain("exactly ONE node")` so the retired instruction cannot creep back. Note the test's own `it(...)` title says "one slice" — rename it to match what it now asserts.

CORRECT THE SOURCE-TEXT ASSERTER. apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-close-readiness.test.ts:18 carries a prose comment stating `runSubmitDecomposition` refuses `nodes.length > 1` as a live premise; it is the third of the three grep hits from step 1 and would otherwise outlive the rule it describes. Rewrite ONLY that comment to say the compiler admits N nodes and that a criterion left unbound by every node still refuses COMPILED_PLAN_CRITERION_UNBOUND — which is the part of the premise that actually still holds and that the file's arms depend on. Do not change any assertion in that file: its arms reach a partial-coverage state via a SECOND contract with distinct criterion ids, which is unaffected by the node count. THIS FILE IS DIRTY WITH PEER WIP (confirmed `M` at plan time). Never revert, stash or `git add -A` it. Edit only the comment lines, and in the step note quote `git diff -- apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-close-readiness.test.ts` to show your change alongside the peer's, so the commit's attribution is honest (global rail 5).

Attribute any red by the merge-base/HEAD delta intersected with this row's five files (global rail 3) and quote foreign red verbatim rather than hiding it. The named verification command for completion is `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. (c) ADVERSARIAL READ, in the note: does anything downstream assume one node per sealed graph — check the compiled-node-source and coverage readers before claiming none; can a dependsOn CYCLE now reach finalize, or does compiled-authority-bodies refuse it first (if a cycle is admissible, say so plainly — the dependency gate in task-1d7b9df2 would deadlock on it); and does the new mission sentence still fit the seat's context budget.

planningNotes.risks: BIGGEST RISK — lifting a count fence without the coherence fence being real. If compiled-authority-bodies' dependsOn checks were weaker than measured, this row would start sealing graphs that finalize or the scheduler cannot execute. Step 3 pins those refusals BEFORE step 4 deletes anything, and step 1 tells the worker to report blocked rather than proceed if core has regained a node-count arm. SECOND — a dependsOn CYCLE. compiled-authority-bodies refuses self-edges and unknown targets, but the plan-time measurement did not establish that a longer cycle (a->b->a) is refused. Step 7(c) makes the worker answer this explicitly, because task-1d7b9df2's dependency gate would deadlock a cycle at the surface rather than refuse it at compile. THIRD — file collision with task-138fab30 and task-957bccf1, both of which own compile-dispatcher.ts. Regions are disjoint and I amended 138fab30's conflicting step, but whichever lands second will rebase onto the other; the amended step and this plan both say the code's absence is expected and must not be restored. FOURTH — goal-close-readiness.test.ts is DIRTY with peer WIP. Its `git diff` is a valid restore proof only because it is tracked. FIFTH — the drill in step 7(a) mutates a TRACKED, clean file, so an empty `git diff` is sound proof; do not carry that shortcut to any untracked path (global rail 13). SIXTH — the mission text is read by live seats: a longer sentence costs seat context, and a seat that misreads it will submit a structure the compiler refuses. Step 7(c) asks the worker to sanity-check the length.
